docs.title: Home
docs.text:
This is the homepage for HandyUI documentation.

You will get introduced to HandyUI and the reason to it's existence here.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Code-only (like WinForms)
  • Uses SkiaSharp for rendering
  • Open Source and free to modify

docs.title: Why it exists
docs.text:
Basically, I (davpnuser) was trying to make a modern, hardware-accelerated GUI app in C# and modern .NET. I tried using WinForms, Uses GDI+. What about WPF? Uses XAML. Well, what about Avalonia? Nope, it has a lot of boilerplate. WinUI Markup? Sucks.

So, i was basically trying to find a option that didnt exist so at one point i got tired and started using SkiaSharp with WinForms. (yes, i know, i was using the exact framework i didnt use at first.) And it was going good until... I realized that WinForms is NOT cross-platform. So, i decided to try using alternatives such as OpenTK's C# library and Silk.NET and etc.

But, ultimately, i found that Silk.NET works best. So, i was then using pure Silk.NET and SkiaSharp for a while until i realized once again, that, there was a lot of boilerplate. So, i began work on HandyUI. At first, it was really incapable. Really. Incapable. Then, over time, it started getting better with more and more updates.

My decision of seperating the core renderer to a seperate library especially helped me out when i wanted to make a Silk.NET adapter. I first made the Silk.NET adapter, and once it got stable enough, i deprecated the WinForms (legacy) adapter.

docs.title: What's next for HandyUI?
docs.text: I can't tell. It has way more features than it used to have, but still, im a solo developer. Don't expect much advanced work from me. I'm a human too, after all. Still, i will be maintaining this package as long as i physically can until i either get burnt out or i take a break. But, you should not expect advanced built-in controls from me. That is your work. You can use a control library; Make a control library. Do what you want but dont expect advanced controls from me.

docs.title: BaseControl
docs.text:
HandyUI.Core.Classes.Base.BaseControl

The base class for every drawable control. It provides transformation, geometry, visual state, interaction state, a parent/children tree, and invalidation events.

public abstract class BaseControl : IControl

Positioning is nullable

Both DoesIntersect and OnUpdate receive SKPoint?. A null value means "the cursor is not over this control's subtree" - this is how the renderer propagates clipping without a magic sentinel value.

When false, the control ignores its Location when resolving absolute positions.

docs.title: ScissoringEnabled
docs.text:
public bool ScissoringEnabled { get; set; }   // default: true

When true, the renderer clips the subtree to Bounds and skips dispatching events to out-of-bounds children.

docs.title: Abstract methods
docs.text:
public abstract bool DoesIntersect(SKPoint? clientPoint);
public abstract void OnUpdate(float deltaTime, SKPoint? clientMousePosition);
public abstract void OnDraw(SKCanvas canvas);
  • DoesIntersect receives a point in the control's local space - or null when the cursor is clipped out of the subtree. Return false for null.
  • OnUpdate runs once per frame before OnDraw. clientMousePosition is local (or null when clipped).
  • OnDraw runs after OnUpdate; the canvas is already translated to the control origin when ParentChildPositioningEnabled is true.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
public sealed class ClickBox : BaseControl<ClickBox>
{
    public event Action? Clicked;

    public override bool DoesIntersect(SKPoint? p)
        => p is not null && Bounds.Contains(p.Value);

    public override void OnUpdate(float dt, SKPoint? mouse) { }

    public override void OnDraw(SKCanvas canvas)
    {
        using var paint = new SKPaint
        {
            Color = IsHovered ? SKColors.Orange : SKColors.CornflowerBlue
        };
        canvas.DrawRect(Bounds, paint);
    }

    protected override bool OnMouse(MouseEventContext ctx)
    {
        if (ctx.Type == MouseEventType.Click)
        {
            Clicked?.Invoke();
            return true;
        }
        return false;
    }
}

new ClickBox()
    .WithBounds(0, 0, 160, 48)
    .WithAddToRenderer(renderer);

public sealed class FrameCounter : BaseModule<FrameCounter>
{

docs.title: Input Contexts
docs.text: Records describing mouse and keyboard events passed to controls.

docs.title: Mouse
docs.text:
public enum MouseButton { None, Left, Right, Middle }

public enum MouseEventType { Move, MouseDown, MouseUp, Click, Wheel }

docs.title: MouseEventContext
docs.text:
public record MouseEventContext(
    SKPoint? ClientPosition,
    MouseEventType Type,
    MouseButton Button = MouseButton.None,
    int WheelDelta = 0);
Field Description ClientPosition Cursor position in the receiving control's local space, or null when the cursor is clipped out of this subtree. Type Which kind of event this is. Button Which mouse button triggered the event (for button events). WheelDelta Wheel delta in "clicks". Typically ±120 per notch.

Null means clipped

Rather than using a sentinel value like (-99999, -99999), ClientPosition is genuinely null when the control is out-of-bounds because of clipping. Custom controls should treat null as "not hovered" and return false from DoesIntersect.

Synthetic clicks

The renderer synthesizes a Click event on MouseUp when the same control was pressed and is still under the cursor.

docs.title: Keyboard
docs.text: public enum KeyEventType { KeyDown, KeyUp, CharInput }

docs.title: KeyEventContext
docs.text:
public record KeyEventContext(
    KeyEventType Type,
    int KeyCode,
    char Character = '\0',
    bool IsControlPressed = false,
    bool IsShiftPressed = false,
    bool IsAltPressed = false);
Field Description Type Key down / up / printable char. KeyCode Virtual key code (Win32-style). Character Printable char for CharInput, otherwise '\0'. IsControlPressed / IsShiftPressed / IsAltPressed Modifier state.

Use CharInput for text

Text boxes should only insert characters on CharInput, not on KeyDown. KeyDown is for navigation (arrows, tab, enter, …).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
protected override bool OnMouse(MouseEventContext ctx)
{
    switch (ctx.Type)
    {
        case MouseEventType.Click:
            if (ctx.Button == MouseButton.Left) HandleLeftClick();
            return true;
        case MouseEventType.Wheel:
            Scroll(ctx.WheelDelta);
            return true;
    }
    return false;
}

protected override bool OnKey(KeyEventContext ctx)
{
    if (ctx.Type == KeyEventType.CharInput)
    {
        _buffer.Append(ctx.Character);
        return true;
    }
    return false;
}

docs.title: HandyWindow
docs.text:
HandyUI.SilkNet.Components.HandyWindow

A window wrapper around Silk.NET's IWindow that runs a dedicated message pump thread, marshals calls with Invoke, and applies Win32 tweaks.

public class HandyWindow : IDisposable

Windows only

The Silk.NET adapter currently supports Windows only. Construction throws PlatformNotSupportedException elsewhere.

docs.title: Construction
docs.text:
public HandyWindow(WindowConfiguration windowConfiguration)

Creates the underlying window on a dedicated thread and returns once the window handle has been created (not necessarily initialized).

var window = new HandyWindow(WindowConfiguration.Default with { Title = "Demo" });

docs.title: Typical usage
docs.text:
Add controls directly to the renderer, not inside OnLoad:

var window   = new HandyWindow(WindowConfiguration.Default with { Title = "Hi" });
var renderer = RendererHelper.Attach(window);

renderer.AddRootControl(
    new MyBox()
        .WithLocation(40, 40)
        .WithBounds(0, 0, 200, 120));

window.Run();

Why not OnLoad?

UIRenderer.AddRootControl is thread-safe and queues the control for the next tick. There's no need to wait for the GL context to attach a control - only things that require a live GL context (like setting the window Icon) need to run after initialization, and those are handled for you through deferred properties.

docs.title: ResourceManager
docs.text:
HandyUI.Core.Components.ResourceManager

A static helper for loading resources from disk or from embedded assembly resources.

public static class ResourceManager

Lookup order

For a relative path (e.g. Assets/logo.png) the manager tries, in order:

  1. AppDomain.CurrentDomain.BaseDirectory/<relativePath> on disk.
  2. The entry assembly, the executing assembly (HandyUI.Core), and any assemblies registered via RegisterAssembly, matching a manifest resource whose name ends with Assets.logo.png.

The first hit wins.

docs.title: WhenErrored
docs.text:
public static Action<string, string>? WhenErrored { get; set; }

Optional callback invoked when a lookup fails and ignoreErrors was false. Receives (detail, path). If null, the manager throws a FileNotFoundException instead.

ResourceManager.WhenErrored = (detail, path) =>
    Console.Error.WriteLine($"Couldn't load '{path}': {detail}");

docs.title: RegisterAssembly(Assembly assembly)
docs.text:
public static void RegisterAssembly(Assembly assembly)

Adds an assembly to the global search list. Idempotent.

ResourceManager.RegisterAssembly(typeof(MyPlugin).Assembly);

docs.title: GetResourceByPath(...)
docs.text:
public static bool GetResourceByPath(
    string relativePath,
    out Stream? resourceStream,
    bool ignoreErrors = true,
    IEnumerable<Assembly>? additionalAssemblies = null)
Parameter Description relativePath Path like Assets/icon.png or a resource name. resourceStream On success, a seekable MemoryStream at position 0. ignoreErrors If false, failures go through WhenErrored (or throw). additionalAssemblies Extra assemblies to check in addition to the global registry.

Returns true if a resource was found.

Stream is a snapshot

Embedded resources are copied into a MemoryStream before being returned, so the stream is seekable and independent of the raw manifest stream - safe to hand to SkiaSharp.

if (ResourceManager.GetResourceByPath("Assets/logo.png", out var stream))
{
    using var data = SKData.Create(stream!);
    using var image = SKImage.FromEncodedData(data);
    // ...
}

docs.title: Theme
docs.text:
HandyUI.Core.Classes.Records.Theme

An immutable-looking palette: a plain C# record with public color fields and a static Default factory. Controls read their initial colors from a Theme and expose per-channel overrides so you can tweak a single color without cloning the whole palette.

public record Theme
{
    public SKColor PrimaryColor          = SKColor.Parse("#2563EB");
    public SKColor SecondaryColor        = SKColor.Parse("#3B82F6");
    public SKColor DisabledColor         = SKColor.Parse("#E2E8F0");
    public SKColor TextColor             = SKColor.Parse("#0F172A");
    public SKColor LightTextColor        = SKColor.Parse("#FFFFFF");
    public SKColor DisabledTextColor     = SKColor.Parse("#94A3B8");
    public SKColor BackgroundColor       = SKColor.Parse("#F8FAFC");
    public SKColor DarkerBackgroundColor = SKColor.Parse("#FFFFFF");
    public SKColor ActiveColor           = SKColor.Parse("#2563EB");
    public SKColor SemiActiveColor       = SKColor.Parse("#DBEAFE");
    public SKColor BorderColor           = SKColor.Parse("#CBD5E1");

    public static Theme Default => new();
}

Fields, not properties

Theme uses public fields rather than auto-properties. That means you can mutate an instance in place (theme.PrimaryColor = SKColors.Red;) - and with expressions still work because the compiler's synthesized copy constructor copies fields as well.

docs.title: Default
docs.text:
public static Theme Default => new();

Returns a fresh Theme instance with the built-in light palette. Because it allocates on every access, cache it in a field if you call it in a hot loop:

private static readonly Theme s_theme = Theme.Default;

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Default Typical use PrimaryColor #2563EB Accent / brand. SecondaryColor #3B82F6 Less-emphasized accent. DisabledColor #E2E8F0 Fill for disabled controls. TextColor #0F172A Primary text. LightTextColor #FFFFFF Text on dark / colored backgrounds. DisabledTextColor #94A3B8 Text on disabled controls. BackgroundColor #F8FAFC Panel / control background. DarkerBackgroundColor #FFFFFF Window background (default canvas clear). ActiveColor #2563EB Highlight for the active / selected item. SemiActiveColor #DBEAFE Hover / soft highlight. BorderColor #CBD5E1 Outline strokes.

docs.title: Custom palettes
docs.text:
Because it's a record, with gives you a new instance without mutating the original:

var dark = Theme.Default with
{
    BackgroundColor       = SKColor.Parse("#131E37"),
    DarkerBackgroundColor = SKColor.Parse("#090C13"),
    TextColor             = SKColor.Parse("#F8FAFC"),
    BorderColor           = SKColor.Parse("#3F719A")
};

var accent = Theme.Default with { PrimaryColor = SKColors.Orange };

Every built-in control exposes Theme as a Theme property and a WithTheme(Theme) fluent method, so a palette swap is a one-liner:

new TextButton()
    .WithText("Save")
    .WithTheme(dark)
    .WithAddToRenderer(renderer);

Custom colors survive a theme swap

When you assign an individual color on a control (e.g. button.NormalBackgroundColor = SKColors.Black;), the control marks that channel as customized. A later WithTheme(...) will only overwrite the channels you haven't touched. This is implemented with private _customXxxSet flags inside each control.

Default is a factory, not a singleton

Theme.Default allocates a new Theme each call. Do not compare references (Theme.Default == Theme.Default is false). The record's value-based Equals compares fields, so Theme.Default.Equals(other) behaves as you'd expect.

UIRenderer uses internal locks and pending-queue lists. AddRootControl, RemoveRootControl, AddModule, RemoveModule, and Invalidate are all safe to call from any thread.

docs.text:

Queues control for addition as a root control. Attachment happens on the next render/update tick.

docs.text:
public void RemoveRootControl(IControl control)

Queues control for removal. On the next tick the renderer unsubscribes from events, clears focus/press tracking, and calls Dispose() on the control.

Ownership

RemoveRootControl disposes the control. If you want to hide it temporarily, set IsVisible = false instead.

docs.title: ProcessMouseEvent(MouseEventContext context)
docs.text:
public void ProcessMouseEvent(MouseEventContext context)

Runs a full mouse pass:

  1. Hit-tests root controls (highest ZIndex first).
  2. Updates _pressedControl on MouseDown and sets focus on the hit control.
  3. Dispatches the raw event recursively.
  4. On MouseUp, synthesizes a Click to _pressedControl if it's still under the cursor.

Nullable ClientPosition

MouseEventContext.ClientPosition is SKPoint?. A null value means "the cursor is not over this subtree". ProcessMouseEvent returns early if the incoming event has a null position; the recursive dispatch substitutes null for clipped descendants.

docs.title: ProcessKeyEvent(KeyEventContext context)
docs.text:
public bool ProcessKeyEvent(KeyEventContext context)

Forwards the event to the currently focused control. Returns the control's return value, or false when no control is focused / the control is invisible / disabled.

docs.title: RenderControls(SKCanvas canvas, SKPoint cursorPosition, float deltaTime)
docs.text:
public bool RenderControls(SKCanvas canvas, SKPoint cursorPosition, float deltaTime)

Processes pending control changes, then draws the whole tree into canvas. Returns true if a render actually happened.

docs.title: UpdateModules(float deltaTime)
docs.text:
public bool UpdateModules(float deltaTime)

Ticks every enabled module by calling module.OnUpdate(deltaTime). Returns true if modules were actually updated.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
var renderer = new UIRenderer(useDirtyRendering: false);
renderer.AddRootControl(myButton);
renderer.AddModule(mySpinner);

while (running)
{
    renderer.UpdateModules(deltaTime);
    renderer.RenderControls(canvas, mousePos, deltaTime);
}

docs.title: Dispose
docs.text:
public void Dispose()

Disposes every root control (recursively), every module, and drains the pending queues. Safe to call multiple times.

Warning

After Dispose, the renderer cannot be reused. Recreate it instead.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
Built-in controls shipped in the HandyUI.Controls package, under the HandyUI.Controls namespace. All of them derive from BaseControl<TSelf>, so they inherit the fluent With… pattern, invalidation, opacity, parent/child tree, and input routing.

Control Purpose CheckBox Toggle a boolean with a box + optional label. Frame A rectangle with a background fill and an optional border. ImageButton A clickable button with an image and/or text. ImageLabel A static image, optionally auto-sized. TextBox An editable single-line text field with caret. TextButton A clickable button that renders a text label. TextLabel A static, non-interactive text label.

Package layout

Controls are not part of HandyUI.Core - they live in a separate NuGet package, HandyUI.Controls. Add it alongside HandyUI.Core:

dotnet add package HandyUI.Core
dotnet add package HandyUI.Controls

Common conventions

  • All controls expose a Theme property of type Theme, defaulting to Theme.Default.
  • Changing a themed color marks that channel as custom, so a later Theme swap won't overwrite your choice.
  • Every control overrides IsEnabled with a backing field that refreshes its paint brushes when toggled.
  • Every control disposes its SKPaint instances in OnDispose.

  • TextChanged / WhenTextChanged fire whenever Text changes (typing, paste, programmatic assignment).
  • Submitted / WhenSubmitted fire when the user presses Enter.

Both channels fire

The event and the Action property are invoked back-to-back. Subscribe to only one per handler, or your callback runs twice.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
A quick heads-up

All code examples in this page use the C# 9 feature Top-level Statements.

Getting started with HandyUI also includes creating a testing window.

You have two options:

  • Create one window

    or

  • Create multiple windows

Creating a single windowCreating multiple windows

docs.title: You can create a window just like this:
docs.text:
using HandyUI.Controls;
using HandyUI.SilkNet.Classes.Helper;
using HandyUI.SilkNet.Classes.Records;

var (window, renderer) = WindowHelper.CreateWindowAndGetRenderer(WindowConfiguration.Default);

new TextLabel()
    .WithText("Hello, World!")
    .WithTextSize(24)
    .WithLocation(15, 15)
    .WithAddToRenderer(renderer);

await window.RunAsync();

Here's the result of running the piece of code given above:

docs.title: You can also create multiple windows at the same time.
docs.text:
using HandyUI.Controls;
using HandyUI.SilkNet.Classes.Helper;
using HandyUI.SilkNet.Classes.Records;

var (window1, renderer1) = WindowHelper.CreateWindowAndGetRenderer(WindowConfiguration.Default with { Title = "Window 1" });
var (window2, renderer2) = WindowHelper.CreateWindowAndGetRenderer(WindowConfiguration.Default with { Title = "Window 2" });

new TextLabel()
    .WithText("Hello, World!")
    .WithTextSize(24)
    .WithLocation(15, 15)
    .WithAddToRenderer(renderer1);

new TextLabel()
    .WithText("Hello World, Once Again!")
    .WithTextSize(24)
    .WithLocation(15, 15)
    .WithAddToRenderer(renderer2);

await Task.WhenAll(window1.RunAsync(), window2.RunAsync());

Here's the result of running the piece of code given above:

docs.title: Creating a window with a custom configuration
docs.text:
You can do this by passing in a configuration object with parameters into the window creation function.

The example i will give right here is changing the title of the window.

To do this, you can create a WindowConfiguration object with the Title property set to the title you want.

using HandyUI.Controls;
using HandyUI.SilkNet.Classes.Helper;
using HandyUI.SilkNet.Classes.Records;

var configuration = WindowConfiguration.Default with { Title = "Your title comes here!" };

var (window, renderer) = WindowHelper.CreateWindowAndGetRenderer(configuration);

new TextLabel()
    .WithText("Hello, World!")
    .WithTextSize(24)
    .WithLocation(15, 15)
    .WithAddToRenderer(renderer);

await window.RunAsync();

Here's the result of this example:

For more info on custom configurations, you can check out the WindowConfiguration page in the API Reference.
